summary: Your cover letter clearly states your interest in the role and mentions your core technical tools, Python and Excel. To stand out, you need to replace generic self-descriptions with specific examples of your project work and directly address the key requirements of the job post.
strengths: Directly states your current academic status as a final-year student, matching the job post's target audience.
Explicitly mentions Python and Excel, which are key technical requirements listed in the job description.

gaps.why: The job post lists writing SQL queries as a key responsibility, but your cover letter does not mention any database experience or SQL skills.
The employer is looking for someone who can build dashboards in Tableau or Power BI, which is currently missing from your letter.
gaps.jobPostEvidence: build dashboards in Tableau or Power BI

gaps.why: The role requires presenting insights to non-technical stakeholders, but your letter only mentions general teamwork without highlighting communication skills.

rewrites.original: I am a hard worker and I am very passionate about data.
rewrites.conservative: I am a dedicated student with a strong interest in working with data.
rewrites.stronger: I am motivated to apply my dedication to working with data, as demonstrated when I [describe a specific project or situation where you worked hard with data] [add the result and its metric, if you have one].

rewrites.original: During my studies I did some projects with Python and I also used Excel.
rewrites.conservative: During my studies, I completed projects using Python and Excel.
rewrites.stronger: During my studies, I completed [N] projects using Python and Excel [add details about what you did in these projects], [add the result and its metric, if you have one].

rewrites.original: I am a fast learner and I can work in a team.
rewrites.conservative: I learn quickly and collaborate effectively within a team.
rewrites.stronger: I learn new concepts quickly and collaborate effectively within a team, as demonstrated when I worked with a team of [N] [add what the team did] [add the result and its metric, if you have one].
